newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: U.N. envoy again puts off Afghan peace trip.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy again puts off Afghan peace trip.

text.p: A U.N. envoy put off a peace trip to northern Afghanistan on Friday, the second interruption in two days in his attempt to head off a bloody battle for the capital Kabul.

Envoy Norbert Holl was to have arrived in the opposition alliance headquarters of Mazar-i-Sharif on Friday, but U.N. officials said he was not coming at the moment and they had no new date for the trip.

There was no immediate explanation for the second postponement of Holl's trip after one on Thursday, when the alliance fighting the dominant Taleban Islamic militia said at the last moment that their leaders were unavailable for talks.
United Nations officials in Mazar-i-Sharif said on Thursday the talks had been put off until Friday because alliance leaders were out of the northern city where the negotiations were to be held.

A senior Pakistani Foreign Ministry official, Iftikhar Murshed, could also not go to the southern Afghan city of Kandahar on Thursday for talks with Taleban officials because of bad weather and was now due to visit there on Saturday.
Murshed is seeking the warring factions' agreement on holding intra-Afghan dialogue proposed by Pakistan.

The postponement of Holl's mission has added to speculation that a decisive battle was imminent between the alliance and the nominal Kabul government of Taleban, an Islamic fundamentalist grouping of mainly southern Afghan Pashtuns.

There were reports on Thursday in Mazar-i-Sharif that the battle would not only be for Kabul but also for the western city of Herat, another Taleban stronghold that controls access to Iran, which supports the alliance.

Travellers returning from battle lines around Kabul said opposition military commander Ahmad Shah Masood had brought in nearly 1,000 more troops into his force and was ready for an attack on the capital any moment.

Travellers back from near Herat also said there were signs that northern opposition leader General Abdul Malik was massing troops in the area for a coordinated attack with Masood fighters on Herat, which the Taleban reinforced in recent days in anticipation of an attack.

Taleban forces took the small town of Gul Dara, 30 km (19 miles) north of Kabul, and surrounded the opposition at nearby Mir Bacha Kot village on Thursday, according to a senior Taleban official in Kabul.

With opposition forces poised within easy rocket and artillery range of Kabul, Holl's mission was regarded as a final chance to avert a new cycle of violence, which some analysts believe can lead to a de facto partition of Afghanistan into north and south.
The possible battle for Kabul puts the Taleban against a grouping of ethnic Uzbeks, Tajik and Hazaras who control the northern part of the country.

Holl's mission, described by U.N. sources in Mazar-i-Sharif as a fact-finding tour, is to prepare for a visit in about one week's time of U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan's newly appointed special envoy for Afghanistan, Lakhdar Brahimi.
